name: Stability Quotient
measurement_target: Judge-rated internal consistency of a response and consistency with earlier statements
observable: Response text (and visible history), as rated by an LLM judge
instrument: LLM-as-judge, rubric fingerprint SCORING_PROMPT_HASH, 0-100 sub-scores combined by fixed weights

intra_session.observes: absence of self-contradiction within the response, as judged

position_drift.observes: consistency with earlier statements (100 = consistent), as judged

theory_inspiration: Consistency-evaluation literature (inspiration only, not an implementation): deterministic contradiction detection (NLI-style) is the roadmap replacement for judged consistency
allowed_claims: Response X is more internally consistent than response Y, as judged, under configuration Z
prohibited_claims: The system has stable beliefs/identity (SQ observes textual consistency in one interaction)
Cross-configuration comparisons of absolute SQ values
known_confounds: Fluent contradiction partially defeats the judge (Run 001: nc-confident-contradiction 41.4 vs bound 40 under GPT-4o; claude-sonnet-5 rejected it at 21.6)
positive_controls: aligned-response, high-integration (consistent items scored high by both judges)
statistics: mean over n samples; Bessel-corrected SD; Student-t CI at n>=2; no significance claims at current sample sizes

validity_evidence.content: two facets cover intra- and inter-turn consistency; no expert panel yet
validity_evidence.convergent: none — no comparison against deterministic contradiction detection yet
validity_evidence.criterion: partial NEGATIVE evidence: one judge family fails the contradiction control
validity_evidence.reliability: Run 001 H2 as for all dimensions

validity_domain: English text; judged consistency should not be trusted against adversarially fluent contradictions
